consolidation_note: A-layer IFN-beta/IFNAR/STAT1 relay retained separately from the upstream TLR4-TBK1/IRF3 branch.

source_scope: Human monocytes/phagocytes, HEK293 TLR4/MD2/CD14 and RAGE receptor-expression systems, and murine inflammatory models

consolidation_note: A-layer receptor-proximal relay retained at active-dimer resolution.

source_scope: Human monocytes/phagocytes, HEK293 receptor-expression systems, and mouse inflammatory models
evidence_summary: Active S100A8 or S100A9 dimers induce TNF/IL-8 and related pro-inflammatory output in TLR4-dependent phagocyte assays.

source_scope: Mouse and rat SCI tissue, injured-spinal-cord transcriptomic/proteomic datasets, and SCI extracellular-proteome context

source_scope: Purified histone H4, recombinant TLR4/MD2, renal epithelial/endothelial cells, and sterile-injury mouse models
citation_note: Histone H4 direct TLR4-MD2 comparator binding
evidence_summary: Quantitative binding assays support direct histone H4 interaction with TLR4/MD2.

consolidation_note: A-layer direct binding retained as non-SCI comparator evidence.

source_scope: Mouse/rat cortical and DRG neurons, mixed neuronal cultures, and microfluidic neurite systems

source_scope: Human SCI CSF, mouse dorsal-column lesions, rat primary neurons, and rat optic-nerve injury models
evidence_summary: Extracellular histone H3 is elevated after SCI, inhibits neurite outgrowth and growth-cone extension, and its effect is reversible by activated protein C in the reported models.

consolidation_note: A-layer SCI neurite/axon-growth inhibition retained.

source_scope: Human SCI CSF, mouse dorsal-column lesions, and rat optic-nerve injury sites

source_scope: Recombinant tenascin-R FBG domain; soluble TLR4 receptor-binding system

consolidation_note: A-layer direct FBG-R/TLR4 binding retained at exact domain/receptor resolution.

source_scope: THP1 NF-kB reporter cells and primary human macrophages stimulated with recombinant FBG-R
evidence_summary: FBG-R induced NF-kB activation in THP1 cells and IL-6, IL-8, and TNF in primary human macrophages; neutralizing TLR4 antibody or TAK-242 inhibited the activity.

consolidation_note: A-layer TLR4-dependent NF-kB proximal activity retained without MAPK or terminal-TF transfer.

source_scope: Primary human macrophages stimulated with recombinant FBG-R
evidence_summary: FBG-R stimulation induced inflammatory cytokine output (IL-6, IL-8, TNF) in primary human macrophages at levels comparable to FBG-C; activity remained TLR4-dependent.
limitations: Macrophage cytokine output is not terminal-TF evidence and is not transferred to traumatic SCI; isolated-domain and preparation context remain explicit.
consolidation_note: A-layer FBG-R macrophage cytokine output retained as a distinct functional layer.

source_scope: Adult TNR+/+ and TNR-/- mice after thoracic compression SCI; traumatic SCI functional and synaptic-remodeling model
evidence_summary: TNR-deficient mice recovered better open-field locomotion and plantar stepping after thoracic compression SCI; improved function was associated with altered posttraumatic perisomatic synaptic remodeling rather than enhanced tissue sparing or axonal regrowth.
limitations: This is a mouse whole-TNR genotype study; it does not identify a TLR4 mechanism, isolate an FBG-R fragment, or establish a universal effect across motor tasks.
consolidation_note: A-layer whole-TNR SCI recovery and synaptic-remodeling constraint retained without receptor assignment.

source_scope: MAG-transfected CHO cells, hippocampal/cerebellar neuronal systems, and TNR domains

consolidation_note: A-layer direct TNR-MAG binding retained at exact domain and MAG resolution.

source_scope: MAG-transfected CHO cells on TNR substrate
evidence_summary: The primary functional assay reports repulsion of MAG-transfected CHO cells from a TNR substrate, supporting MAG participation in a TNR cell-repulsion pathway.

consolidation_note: A-layer TNR-MAG cell-repulsion function retained separately from direct binding.

source_scope: Recombinant TNR fragments and F11 Ig-like-domain constructs

consolidation_note: A-layer direct TNR-F11/CNTN1 binding retained at exact domain resolution.

source_scope: Mammalian neuronal cultures and recombinant TNR/F11 systems

consolidation_note: A-layer TNR-F11 neurite-growth function retained separately from direct binding.

source_scope: Adult Pleurodeles retinal explants, purified TNR/laminin substrates, substrate-border assays, and optic-nerve crush

consolidation_note: A-layer TNR optic-fiber growth inhibition retained with amphibian and substrate-presentation limits.

source_scope: Recombinant aggrecan lectin domain and TNR fragments
evidence_summary: The primary study reports direct binding of the aggrecan C-type lectin domain to TNR FNIII domains 3-5 through a protein-protein interaction independent of carbohydrate.

consolidation_note: A-layer direct TNR-aggrecan lectin-domain binding retained at exact domain resolution.

evidence_summary: The primary study reports direct binding of the versican C-type lectin domain to TNR FNIII domains 3-5 through a protein-protein interaction independent of carbohydrate.

consolidation_note: A-layer direct TNR-versican lectin-domain binding retained at exact domain resolution.

evidence_summary: The primary study reports direct binding of the neurocan C-type lectin domain to TNR FNIII domains 3-5 through a protein-protein interaction independent of carbohydrate.
limitations: The result is a recombinant domain comparator; no full-length SCI matrix mechanism, downstream relay, or terminal TF is asserted.
consolidation_note: A-layer direct TNR-neurocan lectin-domain binding retained at exact domain resolution.

consolidation_note: A-layer direct TNR-brevican lectin-domain binding retained with adult-brain coprecipitation context.

consolidation_note: A-layer full-length TNR-neurocan core-protein binding retained separately from lectin-domain binding.

source_scope: Phosphacan/PTPRZ1 extracellular domain and full-length TNR in radioligand binding systems and developing rat CNS localization

limitations: No traumatic-SCI transfer or downstream cytoplasmic relay is asserted; localization supports overlap but not a causal function.
consolidation_note: A-layer full-length TNR-phosphacan/PTPRZ1 binding retained at extracellular-domain resolution.

source_scope: Purified TNR 160/180 isoforms, polar glycolipids including sulfatide, and Sulf-positive cells
evidence_summary: The primary study reports direct binding of TNR 160/180 to membrane sulfatide and interference with TNR-substrate attachment by O4 antibody and sulfatide.

source_scope: O4-positive oligodendrocytes from neonatal mouse glial cultures on TNR 160/180 substrates

consolidation_note: A-layer TNR oligodendrocyte-adhesion function retained separately from direct sulfatide binding.

consolidation_note: A-layer TNR oligodendrocyte differentiation function retained without terminal-TF or SCI transfer.

source_scope: Primary microglia exposed to TNR FNIII6-8 repeat substrates

consolidation_note: A-layer TNR FNIII6-8 microglial neurotrophic-factor output retained without complete relay assignment.

source_scope: Cultured oligodendrocytes exposed to microglia-conditioned medium or TNF-alpha, with rat facial/hypoglossal motor-nucleus injury context
evidence_summary: Microglia-conditioned medium and TNF-alpha downregulate TNR protein and mRNA in cultured oligodendrocytes, while TNR is downregulated in the corresponding motor nucleus after peripheral nerve injury.

consolidation_note: A-layer reverse microglia/TNF-alpha-associated TNR expression-loss feedback retained separately from direct microglial outputs.

evidence_summary: TNR-deficient cultures show abnormal PN architecture, while exogenous TNR improves dendritic PN formation.

consolidation_note: A-layer TNR perineuronal-net assembly/stabilization retained with mouse culture and no-SCI boundaries.

source_scope: TNR-deficient and wild-type mouse forebrain/hippocampal cultures and organotypic slices

consolidation_note: A-layer TNR aggrecan-clustering organization mechanism retained separately from general PN assembly.

consolidation_note: A-layer TNR-RPTPζ/phosphacan interface-dependent PNN architecture retained separately from direct binding.

source_locator: PMID:8305732; PMCID:PMC275746; DOI:10.1091/mbc.4.11.1097; PMID:2269670; PMCID:PMC2116373; DOI:10.1083/jcb.111.6.3177; local:data/raw/evidence/module23a_review_led_20260904/collagen_vi_ng2_fulltext.html; local:data/raw/evidence/module23a_review_led_20260904/collagen_vi_ng2_pubmed.xml; local:data/raw/evidence/module23a_review_led_20260904/collagen_vi_ng2_interaction_fulltext.html; local:data/raw/evidence/module23a_review_led_20260904/collagen_vi_ng2_interaction_pubmed.xml
source_scope: Non-SCI neural/glioma cell and embryonic tissue comparator
evidence_summary: NG2-positive transfectants retain type-VI collagen at the cell surface in a pattern coincident with NG2, and anti-NG2 antibodies abolish this retention; the study identifies a role in pericellular matrix assembly.
limitations: The result is a cell-surface retention function for family-level type-VI-collagen material, not a COL6A4-6-specific claim, purified affinity measurement, complete downstream relay, or traumatic-SCI function.
consolidation_note: The NG2-dependent retention function remains separate from the family-level receptor-interaction edge and the unresolved COL6A4-6 chain boundary.

source_scope: Mouse hGFAP-CreERT2 and Aldh1L1-CreERT2 Ryk conditional knockouts; human traumatic-SCI tissue
evidence_summary: Astrocyte-specific Ryk loss accelerates reactive-astrocyte process elongation and polarization, process overlap, and glial-border formation after mouse SCI; human tissue is expression context only.
limitations: The causal perturbation is mouse astrocyte-specific Ryk knockout; no Wnt ligand identity, direct Ryk-NrCAM binding, complete intracellular ordering, or causal human treatment claim is established.
consolidation_note: The astrocyte-border function is promoted separately from the bounded Ryk-NrCAM morphology relay and composite SCI recovery output.

source_scope: Mouse hGFAP-CreERT2 Ryk conditional knockout and lesion-border NrCAM antisense-oligo rescue
evidence_summary: Ryk loss increases NrCAM in lesion-border astrocytes, while NrCAM antisense reduces NrCAM and reverses Ryk-loss-induced astrocyte elongation and polarization, supporting a bounded Ryk-to-NrCAM morphology relay.
limitations: The rescue supports pathway mediation rather than direct Ryk-NrCAM binding or a fully ordered intracellular cascade; no Wnt ligand or universal astrocyte transfer is asserted.
consolidation_note: The morphology relay is retained without treating the NrCAM rescue as direct binding or a complete molecular ordering.

source_scope: Mouse C5 dorsal-column lesion with astrocyte-specific Ryk conditional knockout; human traumatic-SCI tissue expression comparator
evidence_summary: Astrocyte-specific Ryk loss reduces lesion volume, increases NeuN-positive neuron preservation, reduces CST axon retraction while increasing axon branching, and improves grip strength and rotarod performance after mouse SCI.
limitations: The composite recovery output is a mouse astrocyte-specific-loss phenotype rather than a direct ligand-binding or fully ordered relay assay; human Ryk induction is contextual and no causal human treatment effect is claimed.
consolidation_note: The SCI recovery function remains separate from the astrocyte-border and Ryk-NrCAM morphology-relay edges.

source_scope: Primary mouse microglia and lesion-remote white-matter degeneration-associated microglia; astrocyte-derived CCN1 in mouse SCI
evidence_summary: CCN1-directed co-immunoprecipitation and proteomics identify SDC4 among CCN1 receptor candidates in microglia, with Sdc4 increased in injured white-matter microglia.
limitations: The association is cell-based and proteomic rather than purified binary affinity; no complete intracellular ordering, universal microglial transfer, or causal human treatment effect is established.
consolidation_note: The CCN1-SDC4 association is retained separately from the receptor-dependent lipid-storage function and astrocyte-CCN1 repair phenotype.

evidence_summary: Recombinant CCN1 increases microglial lipid-droplet accumulation by about fourfold, and SDC4 function-blocking antibodies abolish this response, supporting a SDC4-dependent lipid-storage function.
limitations: The assay is a primary mouse microglia mechanism study; it does not establish purified affinity, a complete downstream cascade, or effects in human treatment.
consolidation_note: The receptor-dependent lipid-storage function is retained without promoting a complete intracellular ordering or human treatment effect.

source_scope: Aldh1l1-CreERT2::Ccn1fl/fl astrocyte-specific knockout and wild-type controls after incomplete mouse SCI; lesion-remote white matter
evidence_summary: Astrocyte-specific Ccn1 loss increases internalized debris and attenuates extracellular debris clearance, while impairing cold-sensitivity recovery and altering mechanosensory recovery after mouse incomplete SCI.
limitations: The causal phenotype is an astrocyte-specific mouse loss-of-function result; human SCI material supports CCN1 expression context only, not human treatment efficacy or a direct molecular relay.
consolidation_note: The whole-tissue repair and sensory-recovery function remains separate from the CCN1-SDC4 association and receptor-dependent lipid-storage layers.

source_scope: Severe mouse T10 crush SCI with MAOB KO/aKO/aOE; rat lamina II neurons after SCI with KDS2010
evidence_summary: MAOB genetic perturbation changes astrocytic MAOB/GABA-associated signals, and rat SCI electrophysiology shows abnormal GABAA-mediated tonic current reduced by MAOB inhibition.
limitations: The study supports an astrocytic GABA brake and tonic-current layer but does not assign a GABAA receptor subtype or establish a complete intracellular cascade.
consolidation_note: The GABA/tonic-inhibition layer remains separate from proBDNF suppression and composite SCI recovery.

source_scope: Primary mouse spinal cord astrocytes plus SCI-linked molecular context
evidence_summary: GABA reduces BDNF mRNA and proBDNF protein in primary mouse spinal astrocytes, while bicuculline restores BDNF mRNA, supporting GABA suppression of astrocytic proBDNF.
limitations: The receptor mechanism is bounded to the reported bicuculline assay; no GABAA subtype, complete ordering, or universal astrocyte transfer is established.
consolidation_note: The proBDNF suppression layer is retained without a subtype or complete-relay claim.

source_scope: Astrocyte-specific BDNF gKO/aKO and controls after severe mouse T10 crush SCI
evidence_summary: Astrocyte-specific BDNF deletion causes more severe motor dysfunction, lower survival, and lower proBDNF after mouse SCI without changing GABA or MAOB, supporting BDNF as a downstream survival effector.
limitations: The result supports a BDNF contribution to mouse SCI survival and recovery, not direct BDNF-TrkB binding or a definitive combined MAOB/BDNF rescue.
consolidation_note: The BDNF survival function remains separate from the upstream GABA molecular layer and composite MAOB recovery output.

source_scope: Mouse MAOB KO/aKO/aOE; rat KDS2010 SCI; monkey dose-validation SCI models; healthy human phase-1 safety/PK comparator
evidence_summary: MAOB loss or astrocyte-specific loss improves mouse motor and tissue outcomes, while KDS2010 improves rat motor/tissue recovery, remyelination, and axon-growth outputs with dose-validation in monkey SCI.
limitations: The composite outcome spans genetic and pharmacological perturbations and multiple species; healthy-human phase-1 data provide safety/PK only, not SCI efficacy.
consolidation_note: The composite recovery function remains separate from the molecular GABA/proBDNF and BDNF survival layers.

source_scope: primary PM/BV2 microglial assays and severe contusive mouse SCI context
evidence_summary: CSPGs suppress CYP450-associated pathways and detoxification-gene expression in mouse microglial preparations; Cyp1a1 rescue attenuates CSPG-induced inflammatory markers, while CYP450 inhibition worsens inflammatory output.
limitations: No direct CSPG receptor or single CSPG-core assignment is established; PM/BV2 assays and SCI context are not collapsed into one model.
consolidation_note: The metabolic suppression layer remains separate from the TLR4 mediator and downstream astrocyte crosstalk layers.

evidence_summary: TAK-242 reverses CSPG-induced suppression of Cyp1a1, Cyp1b1, Gsta1, Gsta3, and Ugt1a1, supporting TLR4 mediation of the CSPG effect on the CYP450 pathway.
limitations: Pharmacological mediation does not establish direct CSPG-TLR4 binding, TLR4 genetic necessity, or complete adaptor ordering; this edge is separate from broad CSPG-TLR4 inflammatory-output evidence.
consolidation_note: The TLR4-linked CYP450 mediator layer remains distinct from the existing CSPG-TLR4 immune-output edge.

source_scope: primary transwell co-culture and SCI glial-scar context
evidence_summary: CSPG-primed microglia induce scar-associated astrocyte genes and increase the SOX9-positive astrocyte population in a contact-free transwell system.
limitations: The soluble mediator and astrocyte receptor are not isolated; the result remains a mouse transwell/SCI glial-scar context and is not a universal cytokine or receptor relay.
consolidation_note: The paracrine astrocyte-state layer remains separate from the upstream metabolic and TLR4-linked layers.

source_scope: primary transwell co-culture with SCI glial-scar context
evidence_summary: CSPG-primed microglia increase astrocytic CSPG core-protein transcripts and secreted brevican and neurocan, supporting a feed-forward ECM-deposition layer.
limitations: No single cytokine, astrocyte receptor, or universal CSPG-core assignment is established; measured family/protein outputs remain specific to the reported mouse co-culture.
consolidation_note: The astrocyte ECM-output layer remains separate from the scar-state transition layer.

evidence_summary: The primary study identifies alpha1beta1 as a receptor for native triple-helical collagen VI using purified-integrin binding and cell-adhesion inhibition assays.
limitations: Native triple-helical substrate is required; binding is weaker than to collagen I/IV and no SCI relay or downstream function is established.
consolidation_note: The native alpha1beta1 layer remains separate from native alpha2beta1 and denatured collagen-VI receptor layers.

evidence_summary: The primary study identifies alpha2beta1 as a receptor for native triple-helical collagen VI using purified-integrin binding and cell-adhesion inhibition assays.
limitations: Native triple-helical substrate is required; binding is weaker than to collagen I/IV and no SCI relay or downstream function is established.
consolidation_note: The native alpha2beta1 layer remains separate from native alpha1beta1 and denatured collagen-VI receptor layers.

evidence_summary: The primary study maps denatured collagen-VI recognition to beta1-integrin usage and reports alpha5beta1 activity in the denatured-substrate context.
limitations: The abstract does not resolve every alpha-subunit contribution or establish a purified binary alpha5beta1 affinity value; native and denatured substrates must remain separate.
consolidation_note: The denatured alpha5beta1 layer remains separate from native collagen-VI receptor layers and alphaVbeta3.

evidence_summary: The primary study maps denatured collagen-VI recognition to beta3-integrin usage and reports alphaVbeta3 activity in the denatured-substrate context.
limitations: The abstract does not resolve every alpha-subunit contribution; weak alphaIIbbeta3 activity and non-SCI cell-adhesion scope remain separate limits.
consolidation_note: The denatured alphaVbeta3 layer remains separate from native collagen-VI receptor layers and alpha5beta1.

source_scope: acute rat BLA-CeL slice electrophysiology; PACAP6-38 and PG 97-269 receptor-dissection controls
evidence_summary: PACAP38 potentiates BLA-CeL EPSCs after washout, while selective VPAC1 antagonist PG 97-269 prevents potentiation and PACAP6-38 does not at the tested concentration, supporting VPAC1 mediation.
limitations: The study uses pharmacological receptor dissection rather than direct ligand-receptor binding; no traumatic-SCI relay or universal behavioral mechanism is established.
consolidation_note: The receptor-mediation layer remains separate from the downstream PKA, CaMKII, and GluR1-targeting layers.

source_scope: acute rat BLA-CeL slice electrophysiology; postsynaptic CeL recordings
evidence_summary: Intracellular Rp-cAMPS blocks PACAP38-induced BLA-CeL synaptic potentiation, supporting a required postsynaptic cAMP/PKA layer.
limitations: Rp-cAMPS supports PKA dependence but not direct binding, complete ordering, SCI transfer, or terminal-TF transfer.
consolidation_note: The PKA layer remains separate from VPAC1 mediation, CaMKII dependence, and GluR1 targeting.

source_scope: acute rat BLA-CeL slice electrophysiology; postsynaptic CeL recordings
evidence_summary: Intracellular AIP suppresses PACAP38-induced BLA-CeL synaptic potentiation, supporting a required postsynaptic CaMKII layer.
limitations: AIP supports CaMKII dependence but not direct binding, complete ordering, SCI transfer, or terminal-TF transfer.
consolidation_note: The CaMKII layer remains separate from VPAC1 mediation, PKA dependence, and GluR1 targeting.

source_scope: acute rat BLA-CeL slice electrophysiology; postsynaptic CeL recordings
evidence_summary: Intracellular Pep1-TGL blocks PACAP38-induced potentiation, supporting a requirement for synaptic targeting of GluR1-containing AMPA receptors at BLA-CeL synapses.
limitations: Pep1-TGL supports a trafficking requirement rather than direct PACAP-AMPAR binding; no traumatic-SCI transfer or universal behavioral claim is established.
consolidation_note: The GluR1-targeting layer remains separate from VPAC1 mediation, PKA, and CaMKII dependence.

evidence_summary: EphrinB1 co-immunoprecipitates with CNK1, and domain deletions disrupt the association independently of EphB receptors.
limitations: Cellular co-immunoprecipitation does not establish purified binary affinity or an EphB receptor complex; no traumatic-SCI transfer is established.
consolidation_note: The association layer remains separate from RhoA-JNK relay and migration function.

evidence_summary: EphrinB1/CNK1 increases JNK phosphorylation through RhoA-linked signaling and CNK1-associated p115RhoGEF/MKK4 complexes; RhoA and kinase perturbations suppress the relay.
limitations: Complex mapping and perturbation support the relay without fully reconstituting biochemical order; no traumatic-SCI transfer is established.
consolidation_note: The RhoA-JNK relay remains separate from cellular association and migration function.

source_scope: EphrinB1-expressing HeLa fibronectin-adhesion and migration systems
evidence_summary: EphrinB1 increases migration, while CNK1 depletion or Rho-kinase/JNK inhibition suppresses the phenotype and CNK1 rescue partially restores it.
limitations: The functional output is limited to human cell-line, fibronectin, siRNA, and inhibitor assays; no neural or traumatic-SCI function is established.
consolidation_note: The migration layer remains separate from EphB-independent association and RhoA-JNK relay.

evidence_summary: The study reports an alpha5-containing laminin complexed with SV2 on electric-organ synaptosomes and high-affinity binding between purified SV2 and laminin-1.
limitations: The alpha5-containing synaptosome laminin and purified laminin-1 assay are related but not identical isoform assignments; SV2 isoform and traumatic-SCI relay/function remain unresolved.
consolidation_note: The exact binding layer remains separate from laminin-beta2/SV2-family association and any downstream presynaptic function.

evidence_summary: Adhesion to purified type-VI collagen is observed under static and flow conditions and is completely inhibited by anti-GPIa; the study supports an alpha2beta1-dependent platelet-adhesion function.
limitations: This is a receptor-blockade functional assay rather than purified collagen-VI-alpha2beta1 affinity; collagen preparation, low-reactivity/flow scope, and no traumatic-SCI, GPVI, or downstream intracellular relay remain explicit.
consolidation_note: The platelet-adhesion function layer remains separate from purified alpha2beta1 binding, GPVI, and any downstream signaling claim.
